item.title: FBI pins $6.3B Binance crypto heist on North Korean hackers
item.description: The FBI has blamed North Korean hackers for the record-breaking $6.3 billion theft from cryptocurrency exchange Binance, pointing the finger at the notorious Lazarus Group as the exchange scrambles to replace stolen funds and reassure customers. In an alert published Saturday , the agency attributed the October 29 attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking operation linked to Lazarus, which has made a lucrative career out of relieving crypto exchanges of their digital assets. Pyongyang was already in the frame before the FBI weighed in. Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Elliptic had linked the theft to North Korea, with TRM reporting that most of the $6.36 billion haul disappeared in about 20 minutes. Elliptic, which puts the total closer to $6.43 billion, says it has verified that $2.85 billion of the stolen assets have been frozen or seized. According to the FBI, the hackers have started swapping their loot for Ethereum, with investigators expecting them to move the funds through decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms and instant swap services to make the money harder to trace. The agency has published a list of cryptocurrency wallet addresses linked to the theft and is urging exchanges, blockchain analytics firms, and other virtual asset providers to block transactions involving the stolen funds. The FBI's attribution comes days after Binance admitted that hackers had made off with roughly $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency. According to the exchange , the trouble started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which gave the intruders access to a service container and allowed them to authorize withdrawals they had no business making. Binance has since resumed customer withdrawals , which it suspended after the attack, and says it has now replenished about 95 percent of the stolen assets. The remaining tokens are proving harder to replace because of their limited liquidity. The exchange has committed billions of dollars from its own reserves and emergency funds to cover the losses, with co-CEO Richard Teng promising that customers won't be left footing the bill. That hasn't stopped users from heading for the exits. Binance recorded approximately $3.64 billion in net outflows after withdrawals resumed, although the company said this represented only around 2.1 percent of its reported assets. Replacing the stolen cryptocurrency is one thing. Getting it back from North Korea is another, and investigators face the considerable task of tracking billions of dollars as the hackers attempt to move it beyond their reach. TraderTraitor has form when it comes to raiding crypto exchanges. The North Korean crew has previously been linked to a string of cryptocurrency thefts, including the $308 million attack on Japan's DMM Bitcoin exchange in 2024 . item.title: Who Checks on the Person Everyone Calls?
item.description: At 11:47 p.m., the family WhatsApp group suddenly comes alive. “Good evening, fam. Please, we have an emergency.” Before the second message arrives, everyone already knows who will be tagged. The eldest daughter who always knows what to do. The brother with the most stable job. The aunty abroad. The uncle in Lagos who “knows somebody.” The cousin with a car. The friend who always picks up, even at an unreasonable hour. In many Nigerian families, care has a name and a phone number. It belongs to the person who pays the unexpected bill, makes the difficult call, accompanies someone to the hospital, settles the family disagreement, or says, “Don’t worry, I’ll handle it.” We call them strong. Responsible. Dependable. We praise their shoulders without asking if they hurt. This is the human question at the heart of AXA Mansard’ s Culture of Care campaign: “ Who cares for the person everyone calls”? The Person Who Always Finds a Way Every family, friendship circle and workplace has one. Sometimes, she is the firstborn daughter who became a second mother long before she was ready. She remembers birthdays, school fees, hospital appointments, and the details everyone else forgets. Sometimes, he is the brother whose first good job quietly turned him into the family’s emergency fund and dependable source. His salary has not grown significantly, but the number of people depending on it has. Other times, it is the mom who serves everyone’s food before sitting down to eat. The father who never admits that he is worried. The friend who listens to everyone’s problems but rarely talks about her own. The colleague who carries the team whenever someone falls behind. These people are often so good at caring that we stop seeing the effort involved. We see the transfer alert, but not the personal plan they postponed. We see the paid bills, but not the hours spent calling doctors, arranging transport, and sitting beside a bed. We see the calm voice saying, “Everything will be fine,” but not the fear or uncertainty behind it. That person everyone calls may also be tired. They may worry about money, struggle with their health, or quietly wonder who would come through for them if they could no longer carry everyone else. Care Has More Than One Currency In Nigeria, many conversations about family responsibility often begin and end with money. Who paid the school fees? Who sent money home? Who handled the rent? Who covered the medical emergency? These questions matter, especially as the cost of living continues to stretch households. But money is only one currency of care. Care can also be time ! The sitting in traffic to pick up someone else’s child; the night spent at the hospital bedside; the regular reminder to an elderly parent to remember their medication. Or listening to the same worry repeatedly because the person telling you has nowhere else to take it. Care can be access ! Advice. Attention. Prayer. Food. Transport. Encouragement. A job referral. A place to stay. A

item.title: Vintage fun: Prodding AI agents using retro hardware just because you can
item.description: From the department of "pointless but still cool" comes word of some kit being repurposed as a terminal for AI agents. AWS developer advocate Darko Mesaroš has connected a teletype to a modern command-line interface to revel in the delight of interacting with today's AI technology via a combination of a DECwriter and fanfold paper, or the display and keyboard of a computer whose heyday ended 40 years ago. Mesaroš' project involved AWS Kiro , a Command Line Interface (CLI) and agentic coding service. We would, however, contend that this is more about seeing what retro hardware can be made to do. Two problems needed solving: getting data to and from the teletype, and formatting the output to work on a piece of kit from another era of computing. He used Hayes modem emulation to deal with the serial connection, and Agent Client Protocol (ACP) for working with Kiro. Mesaroš used a WiModem232 for the former. The device emulates a standard Hayes-compatible modem and, according to Mesaroš, "Folks initially used this to connect Commodore 64s to BBSes in the modern era" (he started his computing journey with a Commodore 64). The latter, getting the Kiro CLI to work on a Teletype, was a little more complicated. Kiro's CLI isn't really suitable for a teleprinter capable of 30 characters per second, after all. A simple Rust application took Kiro's output (obtained via ACP) and turned it into something that a teletype, or dumb terminal, could handle. As we said, seemingly pointless, but making it work required knowledge of Rust, competence with containers, an understanding of ACP, and more than a little creative thinking. So, while one might argue it is pointless from a technical perspective, it is wonderfully educational otherwise. The repository is available and focuses on Kiro for obvious reasons (Mesaroš is an AWS developer advocate after all), but in a chat with The Register , Mesaroš said the concept was portable. He said, "Any coding assistant or any harness that supports ACP, this should work, right? I built it for Kiro, but it uses the standard ACP protocol, so I could easily plug in Claude Code or Codex. Anything that basically can serve as an ACP server should be perfectly fine. "Blessed be the standards, right?" There might be some issues. "The biggest problem with this thing is that it doesn't really handle packet drops at all," he explained. "Like, if you drop packets, they're just gone. There're no retries. It's just spitting information out." And then there is buffering. Or the lack of it. Mesaroš said, "There's actually no buffering happening here. Literally, it just comes down through the fire hose through this serial device, and the bottleneck itself is the serial device." Mesaroš had toyed with using the GPIO pins on a Raspberry Pi, but settled on the serial device instead, since everything worked "out of the box." "It's kind of cheating," he admitted, "but it's also kind of good." Mesaroš collects vintage hardware, with a stash that ranges

item.title: What is Starshield? A look at SpaceX's military satellite network
item.description: null SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them? For more than a week in October 2026, Ukrainian drone operators found their high-speed satellite links shut off. Officials in Kyiv said that terminals for SpaceX ’s Starshield network stopped working at speeds of above 160 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour) from Oct. 14, hampering efforts to conduct defensive operations and intercept Russian drones. Full connectivity was restored on Oct. 24, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The arguments over who did what continue, but the affair highlighted how little is publicly understood about Starshield — what it is, how it relates to Starlink , and how it is operated. What is Starlink? Starlink is SpaceX’s commercial, mass-market satellite internet service. The company says it now has more than 11,000 Starlink broadband and mobile satellites in orbit, operating approximately 342 miles (550 kilometers) above Earth. This follows years of deployment using the company's Falcon 9 rocket.. The network serves consumers, enterprises and government customers across more than 160 countries. It is owned and operated by SpaceX. Anyone from a rural household to an airline can buy a terminal and a service plan. Governments are also customers, with public agencies using Starlink for a range of purposes including connectivity, disaster response and national security, notably in the case of Ukraine in the wake of the invasion by Russia , which began in February 2022 and is ongoing. What is Starshield? Starshield is SpaceX’s network for serving national security customers. The company announced the program in December 2022 , stating it would apply Starlink technology and SpaceX's launch capability to government needs, initially in three areas: Earth observation, communications and hosted payloads. "They are using the same satellite buses," says Bleddyn Bowen, associate professor of astropolitics at Durham University in the U.K. “They look the same, but they have a lot more kit on them that allows them to do more things. They provide similar broadband internet, but with more secure hardware and software and hardened systems.” The company says it has won multi-billion-dollar, multiyear contracts from the U.S. military in 2026 for Starshield-related services. Some Starshield satellites may also carry sensors for intelligence and surveillance. But much about Starshield is secretive, with its finances not revealed and launches often classified. Starshield makeup Starshield is made up of a range of different assets, including spy satellites, military data satellites, and secure communications for ground users. The spy satellites are sent into orbit in launches for the U.S. National Reconnaissance Office (NRO), for a "proliferated architecture" of spy satellites , including electro-optical, radar and relay spacecraft. item.title: Microsoft's moolah mountain is more massive than ever. It just doesn't want the people who built it
item.description: Capitalism can seem so perverse. Take Microsoft, which is celebrating record financial performance by inviting 60,000 employees to consider continuing their careers outside the company . Voluntary redundancy may seem to make sense when a company's running out of cash, but Microsoft is dripping with the stuff . Redmond's first quarter for fiscal 2027 was a bonanza for the tech giant. Its Azure business is up over 48 percent y-o-y, revenues are through the roof, and it has so much moolah it returned $10.2 billion to shareholders in the form of dividends and share repurchases. This latter move probably soothed CEO Satya Nadella, who recently suffered, due to the vagaries of C-suite reimbursement and incentive packages, a 6 percent cut in his pocket money . But as he’s also a stockholder with about 0.01 percent of the company, his share of the cash return presumably eased the pain. He won't have been offered redundo. Jenkins, the large wheelbarrow if you please. Microsoft, then, can afford all its employees, each of whom contributed about $1.5 million to SatNad's bottom line in the last full fiscal year. The "massive efficiencies and RoI of AI" make a great line for a company flogging magic LLM juice, but the evidence remains elusive. AI is, of course, still the reason. Nothing else matters these days. It's just that it's not today's AI. Among all the fulsome figures it put on display for Q1 2027, analysts noted that Microsoft's capital expenditure wasn't as spendy as expected. Quite a lot has been pushed into next calendar year, not because it's not there to be spent – Microsoft could build a 1:1 scale model of the Vatican filled with robot priests if it wanted – but because so much it wanted to mash the Buy Now button for was "Out of stock. More expected soon." This is bad. MS added 88 datacenters in its most recent full financial year: fiscal 2026. That’s not enough datacenters for a cloud business expected to grow by half again in 2027, and hugely not enough to do the other thing. Lags in the cadence of deforestation, dewatering and detonation of the planet can't be tolerated. Thus there are contracts signed to get things back on track PDQ, with mucho, mucho, mucho sponduiks. In its most recent Q1 earnings call, Microsoft is hinting, those selfsame analysts say, that it will have to go to the debt market and go into " negative free cash flow " territory in 2028. In other words, as well as spending its own bank, the company will be taking out massive loans. This is why Billy and Bhavya Dev have to go. The cost of borrowing depends on the financial health of the borrower, and that boils down to how much profit you're making from the money you earn. A big round of redundancies, which are very costly in themselves, sits on the books of the year they happen. The hole in expenditure left by the vanished salaries lives on. The capital must flow. item.title: Britain's driverless dream hits a roundabout of awkward questions
item.description: As robotaxis continue trials in London, an independent research group thinks the UK needs to answer some serious questions before heading any further down the road. To kick off, the sovereignty question, or "Will Britain become dependent on autonomous vehicle services for any key activities and what fallback options will exist if a supplier fails or withdraws?" as the Institute for Driverless Transport (IfDT) puts it. Another question concerns employment: "To what extent does professional driving form part of the UK's employment safety net and how will this function be recreated if demand for professional drivers is significantly reduced?" The objective for IfDT — an independent UK research and convening body focused on the consequences of autonomous vehicles — is to cast the net a bit wider than simply thinking about whether the software is sufficient to navigate London’s wiggly streets and narrow alleys. The research draws on work with operators trying to bring AVs to London and the regulators responsible for policy. It also relied on more than 30 conversations with councils, operators, industry, unions, charities, insurers, lawyers and universities. James Hutt, IfDT co-founder, said: "What struck us most in the interviews was how far this reaches: into jobs, public services, the built environment and national resilience. The people who know those areas best are rarely part of the conversation about AVs. "Our next step is to bring funding and researchers together with the businesses and public bodies that need answers. If you can fund research or offer a place to test it, we would like to hear from you." In August, Transport for London (TfL) granted private hire licences to autonomous vehicle operators provided that a human driver is present during journeys. Wayve and Uber have since launched self-driving rides in the UK capital, with 15 electric Ford Mustangs, equipped with the Wayve AI driver, set to pick up passengers with a safety driver on board. UK company Wayve also demoed a Nissan LEAF , running the Wayve AI Driver using NVIDIA DRIVE Hyperion with self-driving equipment built more closely into the car's design. IfDT points out that Waymo and Baidu are also preparing services for London, while Uber, Pony.ai and Verne have begun testing in Manchester. The research organization said UK authorities still need to answer a long list of questions in order to shape long-term infrastructure plans for local areas and prepare for AI's impact on the labor market. The question of who needs to do this also remains unanswered, as the IfDT asks: "Which are the key public bodies that should already be anticipating the impact of AVs on their own work and who within those organisations should lead a response?"®

item.title: From expertise to intelligence: NISCO deploys world's first swarm-intelligence steel model at scale
item.description: Nanjing Iron & Steel Co., Ltd. (NISCO) has worked with Huawei and ecosystem partners to commercially deploy the world's first steel model powered by swarm intelligence - the YuanYe Steel Large Model (YuanYe) - across multiple scenarios at scale. This helps NISCO transition its core operations from relying on experience to being powered by data and intelligence collaboration. As a traditional manufacturer navigating the challenges of transformation and cost efficiency, NISCO has built a robust digital and intelligent foundation by adopting industry-leading products including Ascend, Kunpeng, Huawei Cloud Stack, and Pangu models. By embedding AI into every core stage of production - ironmaking, steelmaking, rolling, and quality inspection - NISCO is forging green and high-end AI-powered super steel plants. Unlike general-purpose monolithic models, YuanYe innovatively fuses multiple AI models with the steel industry's metallurgical mechanism models to create a dual-drive, multi-model cluster architecture. This architecture features a "right brain" for probabilistic computing and a "left brain" for precise and scientific decision-making. Powered by massive amounts of sensing data aggregated from millions of operational technology (OT) data points across 26 business domains, NISCO has achieved real-time digital twin mapping within its intelligent operations center, laying solid data and scenario foundations for YuanYe. This enables the entire steelmaking process to become not only visible, but also capable of precise control and intelligent assessment. Now 100 percent of NISCO's key equipment is connected and digitally controlled and its new product R&D cycles have been shortened by 50 percent, reducing annual costs by over CNY100m (approx. US$15m). As the model continues to iterate, NISCO had launched 25 business agents by October 2026. These agents cover a wide range of scenarios, from visual quality inspection and process optimization to production scheduling and operations management, setting a new benchmark for digital and intelligent steel transformation. Breakthroughs in four core scenarios: YuanYe redefines traditional operations for significant safety, efficiency, and quality gains In the ironmaking stage, AI makes traditionally invisible blast furnaces transparent. YuanYe leverages blast furnaces' internal sensor data and metallurgical mechanism analysis to perform real-time dynamic simulations of the ironmaking process. Assisted by furnace temperature prediction and health diagnosis models, furnace operators can predict temperatures and identify issues two hours in advance, with over 90 percent accuracy. This shifts furnace operations from reactive post-event remediation to proactive pre-control, increasing prime-grade molten iron yield by over 10 percent while significantly cutting unit energy consumption. item.title: You Should Treat Yourself to a Memorable Destination Birthday in 2027 If You Were Born Between 1977 and 1987
item.description: Christmas is now around the corner, and many of us will already be discussing plans for 2027. Some people will be thinking about new jobs, planning weddings or promising themselves they will finally start exercising next year. Then there are the 1977 and 1987 babies for whom 2027 won’t simply be another year. It is the year they turn fifty or forty, a major milestone in the journey of life that gets everyone asking: “So, what are we doing?” As someone born in 1988, I may not be under pressure to make a similar decision for 2027, but I am close enough to know that my turn is approaching very quickly. And truth be told, the closer I get to forty, the less interested I become in throwing a large party simply because that is what people expect. But after years of travelling, I have also realised that some of the most memorable celebrations are not necessarily the biggest. They are the ones connected to experiences. Like having a private villa breakfast which everyone will always talk about. The boat trip that almost ended with somebody losing their phone in the ocean. The birthday dinner beneath the stars. The destination everyone initially complained was too far, then refused to leave when the trip ended. That is what makes a destination party special. It does not give you one evening. It gives you several days of memories. So, if I were born in 1977 or 1987 and planning a milestone birthday for 2027, I would spend my birthday seeing the world, and these are the destination celebrations I would surely consider, even better if you’re celebrating with your friends: Bali, Indonesia You know that friendship group that has been saying, “Girls’ trip soon,” for the past five years? Every January, somebody opens the conversation again. Everyone agrees. Dates are suggested, then work happens, children happen, school fees happen, someone suddenly has a wedding; something always comes up and halts every plan. Before you know it, another year has passed. A fortieth or fiftieth birthday may finally be the excuse everyone needs, and Bali works beautifully because you can create a luxurious group experience without forcing everyone into separate hotel rooms. Imagine ten friends sharing a private villa with a swimming pool and staff. Begin with a welcome dinner. Add a spa morning, beach club, waterfalls, rice terraces and, on the birthday itself, a private chef and dinner beneath the stars. The greatest advantage of Bali is that luxury can still feel attainable. Just remember that Bali is not the place to invite people who cannot sit still. Some days, the entire plan may simply be breakfast, massage, swimming and sunset. And that is the itinerary . Private villa, poolside dinner, spa morning and sunset beach club–the perfect birthday idea. Thailand Thailand is for the celebrant who wants everything: City energy, beautiful beaches, nightlife, shopping, culture and food. item.title: Rocket Lab launches Japanese Earth-observing satellite on 99th mission to date (video)
item.description: null Rocket Lab launched its 99th mission to date today (Nov. 2), sending a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite toward orbit. An Electron rocket lifted off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site today at 11:41 a.m. EST (1641 GMT; 5:41 a.m. on Nov. 3 local New Zealand time). The mission, which Rocket Lab calls "The Sea God Surveys," is carrying an Earth-observing radar satellite to low Earth orbit (LEO) for the Japanese company iQPS. All went according to plan: The spacecraft was deployed at an altitude of 357 miles (575 kilometers), Rocket Lab announced about 56 minutes after launch. A Rocket Lab Electron rocket launches "The Sea God Surveys" mission for the Japanese company iQPS from New Zealand on Nov. 2, 2026. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) "The Sea God Surveys" was Rocket Lab's 10th launch to date for iQPS, which is assembling a constellation of three dozen synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellites in LEO. SAR satellites offer advantages over those that view our planet in optical wavelengths. They can peer through cloud cover, for example, and study our planet at night as well as during the day. The patch for Rocket Lab's "The Sea God Surveys" mission, which is expected to launch on Nov. 2, 2025. (Image credit: Rocket Lab) Today's launch was the 99th overall for Rocket Lab and the 90th for the two-stage, 59-foot-tall (18 meters) Electron, which gives small satellites dedicated rides to space. The workhorse vehicle has now flown 17 times this year. Rocket Lab's other nine launches to date have been conducted by HASTE , a suborbital version of Electron that allows customers to test their tech in the hypersonic flight environment. HASTE (short for "Hypersonic Accelerator Suborbital Test Electron") debuted in June 2023 and generally flies classified payloads. Editor's note: This story was updated at 11:55 a.m. ET on Nov. 2 with news of successful launch, then again at 1 p.m. EST with news of successful satellite deployment.

item.title: In Photos: Senegal Makes History as the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Kick Off
item.description: Khaby Lame and Boubou Niang take the stage with a young participant at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. If you have been keeping an eye on sports and global pop culture, history was made over the weekend in West Africa. Senegal officially kicked off the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games with a spectacular opening ceremony at the 55,000-capacity Stade Abdoulaye Wade in Diamniadio, marking the first time an Olympic event has ever taken place on African soil. Running through to 13 November, the Games are bringing together over 2,600 young athletes aged 14 to 17, competing across 25 sports and 153 medal events. The action spans three vibrant hubs: the historic capital city of Dakar, the modern satellite city of Diamniadio, and the coastal resort area of Saly. Host nation Senegal enters the arena during the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games Parade of Nations. Under the official motto “Africa welcomes, Dakar celebrates”, the opening ceremony turned into a celebration of music, dance, visual arts, and storytelling. Beyond the parade of nations, the night showcased iconic West African talent. Senegalese music legend Baaba Maal led a massive musical tribute alongside Kiné Lam and hip-hop outfit Daara J Family , while Gambian kora virtuoso Sona Jobarteh and social media star Khaby Lame made featured appearances. item.title: 'Metroid Prime' needs some 'Resident Evil'-style remakes to rediscover its sci-fi shooter mojo
item.description: null Metroid Prime 4: Beyond was, unfortunately, not the return many were hoping for when it finally arrived on Nintendo Switch consoles in 2025. After five years in development at Retro Studios, the original makers of the Metroid Prime series, fans were greeted with annoying side characters, a bike for Samus to roam the barren landscape on, and a deeply unsatisfying ending. It’s a shame, considering how beloved the Metroid Prime series has been since the first title’s 2002 debut for the Nintendo GameCube. Many franchises were jumping from 2D to 3D at the turn of the millennium, and there were plenty of failures — but Metroid wasn’t one of them. The two sequels would enhance how players control Samus with powerful weapons and a multiplayer mode, but the 18-year gap between Metroid Prime 3 and 4 left players expecting something special. Metroid Prime 4: Beyond’s average reception left fans wondering where the series can go next. It’s admittedly strange that Metroid Prime 2 and 3 have yet to debut on Nintendo Switch , either through the Nintendo Online service or as remasters. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake has just dropped for Switch 2, and seeing Nintendo leverage one of the best games of all time for a modern take has given us an idea: let's give the Metroid Prime trilogy the remake treatment, taking inspiration from Capcom’s efforts with Resident Evil. To Prime and Beyond (Image credit: Nintendo) From 2002’s Resident Evil remake to the more recent successes with Resident Evil 2 & 4, Capcom has managed to recreate the feeling and survival horror tropes of the originals while modernizing the gameplay. Whether it's the constant tension of being stalked by a Terminator-like Mr. X in 2019’s Resident Evil 2, or the palpable paranoia you feel exploring in Resident Evil 4 — the skin might be new, but the bones are undeniably "Resi." Even recently-announced Resident Evil: Veronica — whilst a remake of 1999’s Code: Veronica — looks set to be a brand new take that evokes the feeling of the original game, but brings it into the modern era. Prime 4 felt like a game out of time. Sure, it looked the part, but it felt decidedly like a GameCube game. So why not take a leaf out of Capcom's book, apply their "recapturing the vibes" mindset for a Metroid Prime Trilogy Remake, using the Prime 4 engine as its foundation. 2023’s Metroid Prime Remastered showed off the venerable title with better textures and widescreen support, but a remake powered by the fourth game’s engine could showcase the opening and Tallon IV in a whole new light. (Image credit: Nintendo) Similar to 2002’s Resident Evil Remake with the Spencer Mansion, places would feel familiar but fresh, thanks to updated graphics, better sound, and support for HD Rumble 2 that could help the player become more immersed in the game. And of course, you can change a few things to play off people's expectations. If Nintendo is feeling brave, the reimagining could even begin at the end of Zero Missi

item.title: Planetary defense: How military and civil satellites are watching fireballs to help keep Earth safe from space rocks
item.description: null It came from outer space, exploding high above the South Atlantic off the coast of Argentina. That April 1 event — an incoming meteor , also termed a bolide — was observed by both U.S. space-based military and civil sensors. Hush-hush U.S. government satellite sensors detected the speedy fireball cutting through our atmosphere. The object's brightness peaked at an altitude of nearly 60 miles (90.5 kilometers) over the South Atlantic. That dazzling spectacle was also caught by the National Atmospheric and Oceanic Administration's GOES-E and Europe's Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) Imager-1 satellite. Those two independent spacecraft in geostationary orbit detected the bolide via onboard lightning imagers. This skyfall show is among a number of recent episodes that spotlight the value of combining multi-sensor data to not only portray fireball dynamics but also to help appreciate human-caused space debris impacts, as well as strengthening planetary defense knowhow. Hovering in a fixed position high above Earth's equator, the Meteosat Third Generation mission is designed to deliver a rapid stream of data for enhanced weather forecasting. Its Lightning Imager offers a completely new capability for European meteorological satellites, including bolide detection. (Image credit: ESA/Mlabspace) Catastrophic fragmentation Take, for instance, another extraterrestrial incident. In this case, an April 24, 2025 fireball over south-central Alaska yielded one of the most densely recorded "seismoacoustic" datasets ever obtained for a nature-made bolide en route to busting up. A network of 37 seismic stations, 16 single infrasound sensors, and four infrasound arrays recorded 30 ballistic and multiple fragmentation arrivals. All this was complemented by Doppler weather radar detections of falling meteorites and independent optical video observations. Now, toss in for good measure yet another encounter. A roughly 12-foot-wide (3.7 meters) space rock plowed through Earth's atmosphere over northwest Queensland, Australia, on May 20, 2023, accompanied by a raucous round of sonic booms. And U.S. government space-based sensors caught the fall . Researchers later determined that the object underwent catastrophic fragmentation, producing one of the 20 most energetic events reported by NASA's Center for Near-Earth Object Studies (CNEOS) since 1988 and the most energetic seen over Australia. It was equivalent to the explosion of a 7.1-kiloton bomb. An April 24, 2025 fireball event over south-central Alaska. This illustration is a detection map showing a regional seismo-acoustic network in south-central and interior Alaska. Only stations with available data during the fireball event are shown. Green stations denote sensors with detections. (Image credit: Scamfer, L. T., et al.) item.title: Watch Tunde Kelani’s Remastered Agogo Èèwò & Revisit the World of Saworoide
item.description: Official poster for Tunde Kelani’s remastered political classic, “Agogo Èèwò.” If you watched Saworoide , get ready to return to Jogbo. Tunde Kelani ’s political drama Agogo Èèwò (2002), the follow-up to his acclaimed classic, is now available in a newly remastered presentation on TK ÒPÓMÚLÉRÓ’s YouTube channel. Following the fall of military ruler Lagata in Saworoide, the people of Jogbo hope for a new era of peace and prosperity. But the corrupt chiefs have other plans. They install Adebosipo, played by the late veteran actor Dejumo Lewis , as the new king, believing that his background as a retired police officer will make him easy to control as they continue to exploit the kingdom’s treasury. Adebosipo, however, refuses to play along. Determined to protect the people of Jogbo, he demands accountability from the chiefs, setting off a fierce struggle over power, corruption and the future of the kingdom. The conflict reaches a defining moment during a public traditional oath-taking ceremony before the sacred Agogo Èèwò, or Gong of Taboo. Under the custom, anyone who has stolen from the land must confess before the gong sounds seven times, or face the consequences. Written by Professor Akinwunmi Isola and directed by Tunde Kelani, Agogo Èèwò remains a pointed examination of corruption, leadership and traditional systems of accountability. More than two decades after its original release, the film’s return in a remastered version gives audiences another opportunity to revisit the story and its enduring questions about those entrusted with power. The remastered Agogo Èèwò is now streaming on YouTube via TK ÒPÓMÚLÉRÓ. item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 1, 1962: The Soviet Union Launches Mars 1 spacecraft to Red Planet during the Space Race
item.description: null On Nov. 1, 1962, the Soviet Union launched the Mars 1 spacecraft on a mission to fly by the Red Planet. While it did end up flying by Mars , the mission was not exactly a success. After it separated from the rocket, it deployed its solar panels and started cruising toward Mars. When mission controllers were checking out the telemetry it transmitted back to Earth, they found out that Mars 1 had sprung a leak in one of the gas valves that controls the spacecraft's orientation. And without a working orientation system, Mars 1 would have a hard time pointing its antennas in the right direction. It lost contact with Earth when it was about halfway to Mars . A model of Mars 1, a Mars flyby spacecraft launched to the Red Planet by the Soviet Union on Nov. 1, 1962. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Ever since Galileo Galilei pointed his telescope to the red-tinted star and identified as a planet, Mars has captivated scientists' interests as to its nature. So it was of no surprise that as soon as we gained the ability to send missions into space, that the focus turned to the "fourth rock from the Sun." As it turned out, though, reaching Mars, let alone entering its orbit or landing on its surface,, was and continues to be difficult. Mars 1, despite its name, was actually the Soviet Union's fourth attempt at sending a probe to the planet. The first three ended in launch failures. Similar problems faced the United States, as well, but it was NASA's Mariner IV mission that became the first to successfully fly by Mars two years later. Still, as humanity continues to push forward to the day people land on, explore and live on Mars, the 1962 Soviet mission stands as the first to get close to revealing the first details about the planet. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: From Nigeria to Senegal: Ibquake Performs at Historic Dakar 2026 Opening Ceremony
item.description: Ibquake performing live at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games opening ceremony. Senegal came alive yesterday at the opening ceremony of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, with a vibrant celebration of culture, history and African creativity. Among the performers on stage was Nigeria’s very own Ibukunoluwa Aramide Ajagbe , popularly known as Ibquake , who represented the country with a spoken word performance. The ceremony took place at the Stade Abdoulaye Wade in Diamniadio, just outside Dakar, marking a major moment in sporting history as the first Olympic event to be hosted on African soil. More than 1,100 performers took part in the showcase, which featured music, dance, visual arts and spoken word. Senegalese music legends Baaba Maal and Kiné Lam , music group Daara J Family , Gambian kora musician Sona Jobarteh and social media personality Khaby Lame were among the other names featured. Ibquake on stage with dancers and the lit Olympic cauldron at the Dakar 2026 opening ceremony. Stepping onto the global stage in a structured white gown with a sculptural bodice and braided detailing, Ibquake performed against a backdrop of dancers in feathered and textured costumes. Her verses celebrated African identity, heritage and the possibilities ahead for the continent’s young people. Among the lines she delivered were: “We carry a flame for the African child to look beyond the horizon… We are both root and revolution.” Reflecting on the experience, Ibquake shared a personal message online about what being part of the historic occasion meant to her. She imagined her daughter one day asking when the Olympics first came to Africa, and how she would be able to tell her she was there. She wrote: “My daughter will one day ask me when the first Olympics games happened in Africa. And I’ll answer with speed and alacrity. She’ll ask me how I know… And I’ll say… Because mummy was a part of it.” Ibquake surrounded by dancers during the opening ceremony in Senegal. She went on to describe her life as a testament to God’s goodness and reaffirmed her commitment to telling African stories “Powerfully… Boldly,” adding that Africa will always be great in her eyes. The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games run from October 31 to November 13, bringing together approximately 2,700 young athletes from 204 National Olympic Committees and the Youth Refugee Olympic Team. Competitions span 25 sports and 153 medal events, with activities taking place in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. item.title: NASA's Swift space telescope is about to crash to Earth. Where will it fall?
item.description: null NASA's Swift space telescope is expected to crash back to Earth in the next few days. The Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory will reenter Earth's atmosphere in an uncontrolled fashion, after a robotic rescue mission failed to boost the scope to a higher orbit. Swift launched to Earth orbit back in November 2004. Over the next two decades, it studied gamma-ray bursts — the most powerful explosions in the universe — and other cosmic objects and events using a trio of telescopes: a Burst Alert Telescope (BAT), an X-Ray Telescope (XRT), and its Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope (UVOT). On Oct. 20, NASA reported that Swift's orbit had decayed to 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth and that the roughly 3,300-pound (1,500-kilogram) observatory was no longer able to compensate for the effects of the increased drag. It entered safe mode, followed by Swift's operations team at Pennsylvania State University sending a command to the spacecraft that effectively ended its operations ahead of its destructive and fiery nose-dive. It's unclear at the moment exactly when and where Swift will plunge to Earth. But researchers definitely have their eyes peeled. A surge of reentries In physics fashion, for the most part, what goes up must come down — with more space hardware to follow. Thanks to the growing surge in low Earth orbit constellations and technology refresh cycles, there are 10 times more objects reentering per year than there were just five years ago, said Darren McKnight, a senior technical fellow at LeoLabs, a company that keeps a watchful eye on what's going on above our planet. "It is unfortunate that Swift was not 'reorbited,' but from a reentry hazard perspective it is a small portion of the stuff coming back in. The rub on this, of course, is that, while many people bemoan the reentry of more objects , I am much more upset about the rapid rate of abandoning massive objects above 400 miles [644 km]," McKnight told Space.com. Swift will likely disintegrate sufficiently upon reentry to not pose a ground casualty hazard, McKnight said. However, the internal workings of the observatory's X-ray and optical telescope might survive, McKnight said. Where in the world? Similar in view is Dean Sladen, a quality manager and aerospace engineer at the U.K. precision-components supplier Accu Components. "Once Swift falls to about 120 kilometers [75 miles], the end usually comes within a few minutes. The air in front of it heats up so much that the satellite will start to glow. Solar panels and antennas are typically the first to tear off, and at around 78 kilometers [48 miles], roughly eight times the height of a passing airliner, the main body breaks apart. Most of it will melt and vaporize," said Sladen. While it isn't yet known exactly where any surviving pieces will land, Sladen noted that Swift's orbit only passes over a band within about 21 degrees of the equator. item.title: Why you should treat charisma as a red flag
item.description: Today’s crop of smooth talkers tap directly into a specific evolutionary vulnerability. Here’s how to defend yourself Recently, I was alone in a bar waiting for a friend. To pass the time, I started chatting to a stranger. He had an easy, confident way of speaking, which I admired. We discussed topics I know little about: the instability of modern economies, the feasibility of commercial space travel, the likelihood of a coup in Russia. I found myself leaning in and asking questions: I felt as if I could learn a lot from this person. We eventually got to psychology, which is more my wheelhouse. I brooded about how easy it’s become for people to accept strange ideas. “Some people will believe anything,” he observed. “Some people even believe the Earth is round !” It’s increasingly difficult to ignore how fragmented and bizarre our beliefs have become. We live in our own echo chambers, defined by the channels, feeds and influencers we follow. As a result we can arrive at very polarised conclusions about vaccines, the climate, gender, geopolitics, the shape of the Earth and everything else. Disagreements on topics like these frequently damage relationships, alienate friends and estrange loved ones. Continue reading...

item.title: 5 bright planets to spot in November — when and where to see them
item.description: null This is a great month for planet watching, either in the evenings or mornings. During convenient evening hours, the planet of choice is Saturn , visible well up in the southern sky during mid-to-late evening hours. Telescopically, the southern side of its famous ring system is currently tilted about 6½ degrees to our line of sight. Around the middle of the night, Mars and Jupiter come into view above the east-northeast horizon and just before the break of dawn are in excellent position, soaring high in the southern sky in the vicinity of the Sickle of Leo the Lion. Watch how Mars approaches Jupiter early in the month, passes it on Nov. 16, then spends the rest of the month sailing away to the east. Meanwhile, in the predawn morning sky, Venus literally vaults into prominence as the month progresses. And from midmonth on through the end of November, Mercury asserts itself, appearing as a very bright "star" to the far lower left of Venus. In our schedule, remember that when measuring the angular separation between two celestial objects, your clenched fist held at arm's length measures roughly 10 degrees. Here, we present a schedule below which provides some of the best planet viewing times as well directing you as to where to look to see them Reminder: On Nov. 1 — where applicable — change clocks back one hour from Daylight Saving Time. On this date, the clock hour from 1 to 2:00 a.m. is repeated, thus making this day the longest of the year: 25 hours long. The mnemonic is: " Spring Ahead, Fall Back." Mercury Mercury, hidden during inferior conjunction with the sun on Nov. 4, will emerge in the eastern morning sky after the second week of the month to undergo an excellent morning apparition for the Northern Hemisphere. This rocky little world arrives at its greatest western elongation (20 degrees) from the sun on Nov. 20; its most favorable morning apparition of the year for mid-northern observers. From Nov. 16 to Nov. 26 speedy Mercury will rise in the east-southeast before the beginning of astronomical twilight, more than 95 minutes before sunrise. Venus Venus is a good reason to be up at the crack of dawn in November; it's a silvery lamp that rises above the east-southeast horizon. Venus was at inferior conjunction on Oct. 24. But the steep angle of the ecliptic at dawn in late autumn helps Venus vault noticeably higher with each passing day for observers at mid-northern latitudes. On Nov. 1, it rises 55 minutes before the sun. But just several days later on Nov. 5, viewers around 40 degrees north latitude can see Venus come up one hour and 25 minutes before the sun and shine 15 degrees above the horizon at sunrise. As November ends, Venus rises nearly 3½ hours before the sun and hangs nearly 35 degrees up at sunrise. All month Venus brightens impressively and on the penultimate day of the month it will reach the pinnacle of its magnificent brightness, shining at magnitude -4.9, rising almost 3½ hours before the sun. item.title: 9 nightmarish sci-fi spaceships to crawl aboard for Halloween if you dare
item.description: null Abandoned, possessed, or infested spaceships in sci-fi films, books, and video games are usually not a welcoming place to hang your helmet and kick back inside. Many are distinctly marked as DO NOT APPROACH zones and equipped with clearly articulated warning messages to keep your distance, but that doesn't ever seem to stop scavengers, space pirates, or evil industrial mega corporations from waving off these dangerous signs to board anyway. Other creaky craft are apt to contain nasty alien hitchhikers or biological hazards not exactly conducive to a pleasant star-trekking voyage. Whether these nefarious neglected craft have just reappeared from the other side of a black hole or have been lying dormant for eons on a hostile planetoid, visitors are usually infrequent. So ignore those distress beacons at your own peril and step into this alarming armada of 9 nightmarish sci-fi spaceships before orbits decay. Happy Halloween! 1. USG ISHIMURA — "DEAD SPACE" (2008) "Dead Space's" wicked Planet Cracker-class starship, the USG Ishimura (Image credit: Electronic Arts) It's basically a perfectly good interstellar mining vessel owned by the Concordance Extraction Corporation if you forget about the nasty reanimated corpses found lurking on nearly every deadly deck. The pesky Necromorphs are a resilient crop of creatures and are extremely inhospitable when it comes to having uninvited guests, yet they don't mind if you're staying for dinner. This plague of hungry zombified corpses is a real drag, unless you happen to have a flaring plasma cutter in your back pocket and your name is Isaac Clarke. 2. THE GRENDEL — "JASON X" (2002) "Jason X" might have a preposterous premise, but we dig its outer space mayhem (Image credit: New Line Cinema) Things would be much more peaceful aboard the Grendel if a notorious undead slasher named Jason Voorhees wasn't stashed in the cargo bay, but when scientific discovery enters the equation, many questionable choices follow. The Grendel is a 25th-century medical research vessel on a field trip from hell to an overly polluted Earth, where the frozen Jason is kept at the Crystal Lake Research Facility and shipped back home to Earth 2 for cellular research. Once thawed, the ship becomes his private killing field with an ample supply of student bodies until the fiery finale when Jason becomes an inhuman meteor in the sky. Next time, take the school bus. 3. RAMA — "RENDEZVOUS WITH RAMA" (1973) Concept art for the cylindrical Rama spaceship from "Rendezvous With Rama" (Image credit: Google) This spooky classic novel written by "2001's" legendary author, Arthur C. Clarke, focuses on a massive alien spaceship entering Earth's atmosphere. The 31-mile-long cylindrical spaceship does not parallel park easily and is quite spacious inside. In fact, it’s primarily hollow at first and likely offers up a fantastic location for some echoey yodeling. As we later learn, Rama aliens are apparently collecting forms of intelligent life from ar

item.title: This Week In Space podcast: Episode 234 — Living in Lunar Caves
item.description: null On Episode 234 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Mike Wall are joined by Than Putzig of the Planetary Science Institute about a NASA-backed payload bound for the Marius Hills Pit on the moon. In our ongoing quest to develop a moon base, could we possibly utilize the area beneath the surface of the moon in order to make the moon habitable? Could Marius Hills Pit, a roughly 50-meter-wide opening that may lead into a lunar lava tube, become the Moon's first living habitat for humans? Putzig explains how geophysical instruments on a rover could detect hidden voids beneath the surface and measure the size of these lava tubes. We also ask Than how these lava tubes form, what a follow-up robotic explorer could reveal, and how this research fits alongside NASA’s Artemis plans for a south polar moon base. Join us! item.title: On this day in space! Oct. 31, 2015: Creepy skull-shaped Halloween asteroid flies by Earth, NASA names it the 'Great Pumpkin'
item.description: null On October 31, 2015, an asteroid shaped like a human skull flew by Earth. It arrived with excellent timing on Halloween, which made the already-creepy asteroid even creepier. During its closest approach, the creepy asteroid was about 300,000 miles from Earth, or 1.3 times the average distance between Earth and the moon . So, it didn't pose a threat to our planet. It was discovered by astronomers at Hawaii's Pan-STARRS observatory only three weeks before the flyby, and it was given the official designation "2015 TB145." But no one knew what it looked like until the day before Halloween, when the Arecibo Observatory in Puerto Rico captured the first radar images. NASA called the asteroid the "Great Pumpkin," while others called it the "Halloween Asteroid." (Image credit: NAIC-Arecibo/NSF) Why it mattered Be afraid, be very afraid... Okay, not really, but there is reason to be concerned about near-Earth objects and the time in which they are detected. "According to the catalog of near-Earth objects (NEOs) kept by the Minor Planet Center, this is the closest currently known approach by an object this large until asteroid 1999 AN10, at about 2,600 feet (800 meters) in size, approaches at about 1 lunar distance (238,000 miles from Earth) in August 2027," NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) reported in 2015. NASA’s Near-Earth Object Observations Program, sometimes called “Spaceguard,” works to catalog these type of objects and predicts some of their paths if they could be potentially threats to our planet. While there are no known credible impact threats to date, it doesn't mean the "Great Pumpkin," or rather a great impactor, isn't real. These eight individual radar images of asteroid 2015 TB145 were captured on Oct. 31, 2015 using NASA’s DSS-14 antenna in Goldstone, California and the Green Bank Telescope in West Virginia. NASA/JPL-Caltech/GSSR/NRAO/AUI/NSF The Halloween Asteroid 2015 TB145, shown here in an artist’s illustration, whizzed by Earth on Nov. 11, 2018. JOSÉ ANTONIO PEÑAS/SINC As for 2015 TB145, it did return to Earth's vicinity in 2018, but at a much more distant pass of about 24 million miles (38 million kilometers), "or about a quarter the distance between Earth and the sun," according to JPL. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: The moon, Mars, and Jupiter shine in the heart of the Lion overnight on Nov. 1-2
item.description: null The moon dives towards the glowing heart of the constellation Leo for a spectacular rendezvous with Mars and Jupiter overnight on Nov. 1-2, as the glittering stars of the Beehive Cluster shine nearby. Here's what you need to know. Look to the eastern horizon an hour after midnight to see the 45%-lit waning moon shining less than 5 degrees from the red light of Mars — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length to the night sky. Jupiter's bright light will gleam just below the red planet, with the bright star Regulus lining up beyond to form a dazzling procession leading back to the horizon. The stars of the Beehive Cluster (M44) can be found twinkling 10 degrees from the unlit side of the lunar disk around this time, in the middle of the constellation Cancer . Stargazers in Australia, Indonesia and a host of other island nations and territories will see the moon pass directly in front of Jupiter , hiding its light in an event known as an occultation starting at 3:45 p.m. EST (2045 GMT) on Nov. 2 , according to In-The-Sky.org . However, the exact visibility and timings depend on location. The cosmic pile-up serves as a spectacular reminder of the scale and diversity of targets on display in the night sky. After all, the moon appears largest from our Earthly perspective, but in reality it's less than half the diameter of Mars. A simulation of the night sky showing the locations of Mars, Jupiter, the moon and Regulus on the night of Nov. 1-2 (Image credit: Starry Night Pro 8) Jupiter, meanwhile, is over 20 times wider than the red planet, while mighty Regulus is up to four times larger than the sun , andcould easily fit all the planets of the solar system in its vast expanse. By moonrise on the night of Nov. 3, the lunar crescent will have leapt past Jupiter and Mars, to appear just 1 degree from the blue-white light of Regulus for viewers in the U.S. Meanwhile, viewers in several South American countries including Brazil, Peru, Argentina and Bolivia will see the moon occult Regulus beginning at 6:59 EST (1024 GMT) on Nov. 3. The exact timings for a selection of South American countries can be found below, courtesy of In-The-Sky.org . Start time for the lunar occultation of Regulus Country Time in GMT Brazil 07:01–09:03 Argentina 07:15–09:03 Chile 07:07–08:55 Colombia 07:09–07:38 Want to get a closer look at the moon and planets of the solar system? Then be sure to check out our picks of the best telescopes and binoculars for exploring the night sky , including the Celestron NexStar 8SE , which we rank as the best motorized telescope out there. item.title: ONGA Celebrates Nigeria’s Diverse Food Culture with ‘Cook Your Way With ONGA’ World Food Day Activation
item.description: ONGA , the seasoning brand from Promasidor Nigeria , marked World Food Day with its three-day Cook Your Way With ONGA activation, bringing shoppers together to explore Nigeria’s diverse food cultures and celebrate the individual touches that make every meal their own. Rooted in ONGA’s Taste of Home platform, the campaign recognizes that home is not defined by one recipe or a single way of cooking. It is found in the meals people prepare their own unique way and share with loved ones, and in the everyday food experiences that bring comfort and connection. Through the campaign, ONGA is celebrating how people cook their food, not just what they cook, while highlighting its improved ONGA Chicken and Beef seasoning cubes as ingredients that make those meals enjoyable. The activation kicked off on World Food Day, Friday, October 16, and was executed through Sunday, October 18, 2026, at Jendol Ikorodu, Akasolori, on Friday; Ikeja City Mall on Saturday; and Jendol Ibeju-Lekki on Sunday. Across the three locations, shoppers explored the food cultures of Nigeria’s six regions through regional food sampling, interactive games, and culinary challenges At the ONGA Home booth, consumers experienced the taste of different homes such as Native Rice of the South-South region, Suya & Masa of the North-West region, Abacha of the South-East region, Dan Wake of the North-East region, Ofada & Ayamase of the South-West region, Jollof rice of the North-Central region, and took part in the “Cook Your Way With Onga” plate building game, which challenged them to match ingredients to a Nigerian dish against the clock. Shoppers also shared stories about what makes their food uniquely theirs, while showing off their culinary skills through a cooking competition, and had opportunities to win rewards through the several interactive experiences at the event. Speaking on the campaign, Omotayo Olaobaju , Category Manager, Culinary at Promasidor Nigeria, stated: “World Food Day Cook Your Way with Onga campaign was a fantastic platform to engage directly with our consumers online and offline. Onga believes that cooking is personal, and there is no standard recipe for great-tasting meals. Our role as a culinary partner is to inspire cooking confidence in every home ensuring that whichever recipe you choose, the improved Onga Beef or Chicken cube delivers guaranteed richness and taste She also highlighted the ongoing digital challenge as another way for consumers to participate beyond the physical activations. The celebration continues online, where consumers can take part in the Cook Your Way with Onga digital challenge for a chance to win prizes including a kitchen makeover, an iPhone 18 Pro, a fridge and other rewards by sharing their unique ways of cooking their favourite meals on www.ongatasteofhome.com . item.title: Virgin Atlantic Marks 25 Years in Nigeria – Honours Travel Partners
item.description: L-R: Georgia Mobsby, Senior Manager – Sales Excellence; Anthony Uphill, Vice President Sales; Dave Geer, Chief Commercial Officer; Yann Stirton, Country Manager – West Africa; and Liezl Gericke, Head of International, all of Virgin Atlantic, at an awards evening in Lagos celebrating the airline’s 25 years of operations in Nigeria on 22nd October 2026. British international airline Virgin Atlantic marks 25 years of operations in Nigeria with a special awards evening in Lagos, recognising the travel partners whose contributions have helped sustain and grow the airline’s presence in the country over the past quarter of a century. Held at The George Lagos Hotel on Thursday, 22 October, the event brought together Virgin Atlantic executives, travel industry partners and other stakeholders to commemorate a journey that began in July 2001, when the airline launched its Lagos service with four weekly flights operated by a Boeing 747. Speaking at the celebration, Virgin Atlantic’s Chief Commercial Officer, Dave Geer , described Nigeria as one of the airline’s most important and established markets within its international network, paying tribute to the travel partners, customers, employees and operational partners who have contributed to its success. “Technology will never replace relationships. The trust, local knowledge, and customer understanding represented in this room remain fundamental to our success,” Geer said. He also emphasized the importance of building sustainable partnerships, strengthening customer relationships and ensuring that the airline’s investments continue to support long-term commercial growth. Virgin Atlantic’s Country Manager – West Africa, Yann Stirton , acknowledged the resilience of Nigerian travel partners, particularly through periods of economic uncertainty, currency volatility and restrictions on ticket inventory. Highlighting a significant shift in the airline’s commercial performance, Stirton revealed that ticket sales in Nigeria now generate more revenue for the Lagos route than sales in any other market, including the United Kingdom. “When I arrived in Lagos in September 2023, most of the revenue on this route was sold in the UK. Today, more revenue on this route is sold here in Nigeria than anywhere else in the world,” he said. “That didn’t happen by accident. It happened because of the people in this room,” he added. Stirton thanked travel partners for their continued support through challenging market conditions and expressed confidence in building on the relationship in the years ahead. item.title: Betelgeuse is haunted by a cosmic poltergeist tormenting the doomed star's atmosphere
item.description:
Sharmila Kuthunur is an independent space journalist based in Bengaluru, India. Her work has also appeared in Scientific American, Science, Astronomy and Live Science, among other publications. She holds a master's degree in journalism from Northeastern University in Boston. 

Something spooky is stirring in the shadows of the infamous star Betelgeuse, a cosmic poltergeist that is disrupting the atmosphere of the red supergiant. New radio observations have shown Betelgeuse's smaller stellar companion, Siwarha (not Betelguese Betelguese, unfortunately), cutting through the supergiant's extended atmosphere and leaving a wake in its path, like a jet boat slicing through a lake. Because the name of this red supergiant star located about 650 light-years away from Earth, marking the shoulder of constellation Orion, is Betelgeuse, which means "the hand of al-Jawza" in Arabic, the companion was named Siwarha , meaning "her bracelet." "This companion is orbiting so close to the star that it actually passes through its extended atmosphere," Lynn Matthews, the principal research scientist at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) Haystack Observatory who led the new observations, said in a statement . Astronomers turn cosmic ghost hunters Using data collected from 2021 to 2026 using the Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array in New Mexico and the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array ( ALMA ) in Chile, Matthews and colleagues found that Betelgeuse's atmosphere stretches into an egg shape when the companion star is farthest away and rounds out when the companion passes in front of or behind it. The same data also showed that Betelgeuse itself has largely recovered from the " Great Dimming " that made headlines in 2020. This recovery comes after the red supergiant "sneezed" in 2020, dramatically ejecting tons of gas and dust and fading to its dimmest in more than a century. ALMA captures a stunning image of the doomed star Betelgeuse (Image credit: ALMA(ESO/NAOJ/NRAO)/W. Dent et al.) Among the long-standing mysteries of Betelgeuse, scientists have puzzled over a brightening and dimming cycle that lasts roughly 2,100 days. Recent studies pointed to a low-mass companion orbiting deep inside the star's atmosphere, and its existence was confirmed in early 2026 . Though Siwarha itself is too faint to detect directly at radio wavelengths, its influence shows up in the star's shape, the new study found. To confirm the effect, the researchers say, they will need to observe more of the companion's orbit, especially at radio frequencies that have so far been sparsely sampled. The Next Generation Very Large Array , a planned telescope, should make this kind of monitoring far more routine, according to the team. With sharper vision, researchers could see how red supergiants like Betelgeuse shed their material as they near the end of their lives, and how a close companion might affect that process by tugging on that ejected matter. item.title: Halloween night sky 2026 — Saturn, shooting stars and a space station await US stargazers
item.description: null There could be more than just ghosts and ghouls lurking in the skies this Halloween! From Saturn's spectacular rings to shooting stars and even a space station flyover, the night sky has a few treats of its own in store for U.S. skywatchers on Oct. 31. Based on the latest national forecast, skies will be mainly clear on Saturday evening over most of New York State, northeast Pennsylvania, northern New Jersey and New England as well as a swath of the southern and central Great Plains, central Rockies, a portion of the Pacific Northwest and central and south Florida, as costumed kids arrive at the door looking for candy or some other Halloween treat. Temperatures will be mostly in the chilly 40s across the Northeast US, upper 50s and 60s for the nation's midsection, warm 70s to near 80 for the southern US, including Florida and the Gulf Coast, and 40s for much of the western US. Unfortunately, a storm moving across the nation's heartland may spell rainy skies for parts of Iowa and Nebraska, south to the Gulf Coast. For those blessed with a generally fair evening, there will be views of mid-autumn stars and constellations plus a bright planet shining prominently in the early evening sky. If you plan to accompany children around your neighborhood, you might want to enlighten them by pointing out some of those objects that will be visible in the sky. Better yet, if you have a telescope, give your visitors a treat of a different kind: Give them a close-up view of some of those celestial sights. A NOAA map of the contiguous U.S. depicting cloud cover percentages, valid for 7 p.m. EDT on Oct. 31. About 40%of the nation should have clear-to-partly cloudy skies for viewing the evening sky. (Image credit: NOAA/National Weather Service) At the top of the viewing list: The lord of the rings At around 7 p.m. local time, tell your young audience to make a clenched fist with their hands and then hold them out at arm's length. Now, tell them to go "two fists" up from the east-southeast horizon and they will see a bright star, shining with a yellow-white hue. Now, direct your telescope toward that "star" and when you gaze through the eyepiece, you will not be looking at a star at all . . . but a planet! Saturn. This sixth planet out from the sun , just might be the most beautiful of all. Its rings are still readily evident, although currently they appear somewhat edge-on with the south face tilted only about 6 and a half degrees to our line of sight. A telescope magnifying 30-power will bring them out; they appear to bisect the ball of the planet. While this is far from their appearance compared to other years, the view should still look impressive to those who have never seen the ringed planet for themselves. And watch out for fireballs! Because they are active over Halloween, the Taurid meteor shower is sometimes called the " Halloween Fireballs ." The bits of debris that make up the Taurids are a little larger than average, so they can result in brighter m

item.title: Happy Halloween! SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites to orbit from California (video)
item.description: null SpaceX celebrated Halloween with an early-morning launch from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today (Oct. 31) at 12:04 a.m. EDT (0404 GMT; 9:04 p.m. on Oct. 30 local time), sending 27 of the company's Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO). The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth as planned, touching down about 8.5 minutes after launch on the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches 27 Starlink satellites from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base just after midnight ET on Oct. 31, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) It was the 18th flight for this particular booster, which is designated B1093. The record for a SpaceX first stage is 37 , set this past August by the booster B1067. The Falcon 9's upper stage did its job as well today, deploying the 27 Starlink satellites into LEO about 62 minutes after launch. They're joining more than 11,000 spacecraft in the Starlink megaconstellation, which is by far the largest satellite network ever assembled. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship shortly after launch on Oct. 31, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster 1093 launches SDA-T1TL-B | SDA-T1TL-C | Transporter-16 | 14 Starlink missions Today's launch was the 118th Falcon 9 flight of 2026 so far. More than 70% of these missions have been devoted to building out the Starlink network. SpaceX has also launched its Falcon Heavy and Starship rockets three times apiece this year. Falcon Heavy is an operational vehicle, but Starship remains in the test-flight phase. The company is currently gearing up for another Starship launch , which is expected to take place sometime in November.

item.title: The world mourns the passing of 'Star Trek's' Patrick Stewart with a galaxy of tearful tributes
item.description: null As we all begin to absorb the bitter news of Patrick Stewart's death at the age of 86, a flood of personal tributes are pouring in, reflecting this global treasure's wonderful life lived with a dignity and bravado that few mortals possess. We’re getting just a hint of what Patrick Stewart meant to those who worked with him or knew him throughout his stellar career. Whether on stage with the Royal Shakespeare Company, on TV as the dashing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in " Star Trek: The Next Generation ," and in Hollywood spectacles like 1984's "Dune," four " Star Trek " feature films, and the many "X-Men" movies in which he portrayed Professor Charles Xavier, Stewart was always the consummate professional. His final screen performance arrives on Dec. 18 with "Avengers: Doomsday" where he’ll present his Charles Xavier character once more. "Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end," Ian McKellen wrote on Instagram of his "X-Men" co-star and friend. "You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love." Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellan in 2000's "X-Men." (Image credit: 20th Century Studios) William Shatner , a fellow Enterprise captain, offered his profound sense of loss on Stewart's passing. The legends shared the screen in 1994's "Star Trek: Generations." "What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor," Shatner posted on Facebook . "From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work. My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed." Patrick Stewart and William Shatner star in 1994's "Star Trek: Generations." (Image credit: Paramount) Akiva Goldsman, co-creator of Paramount+'s " Star Trek: Picard " and "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds," delivered a sorrowful message in the aftermath of Stewart's death "Patrick was not only a true lion of the profession, he was the rarest of alchemists, one who could literally turn the written word into flesh and blood," Goldsman wrote. "Patrick was kind, strong, fiercely intelligent, collaborative, vulnerable and wise. His Captain Jean-Luc Picard permanently expanded the universe of 'Star Trek' without measure. He will be deeply missed by this one fan and by so many more." Stewart's "Star Trek: The Next Generation" family shared their grief and offered up poignant words to try to describe what effect he had on their lives and profession. "There's no one on this planet that I have acted
